passages.text: In those days when the disciples were increasing in number, the Grecian Jews among them began to grumble against the Hebraic Jews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.
passages.sermon:
The disciples were increasing in number during those days.
Some of the believers were Grecian Jews.
Some of the believers were Hebraic Jews.
The Grecian Jews began to complain against the Hebraic Jews.
Their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.
The Grecian Jews noticed this problem.
They grumbled because their widows did not receive food each day.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ἐγένετο γογγυσμὸς τῶν Ἑλληνιστῶν πρὸς τοὺς Ἑβραίους ὅτι παρεθεωροῦντο ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ τῇ καθημερινῇ αἱ χῆραι αὐτῶν

passages.text: So the Twelve summoned all the disciples and said, “It is unacceptable for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.
passages.sermon:
The Twelve apostles led the early church.
They called together all the disciples.
The Twelve spoke to the group.
They said, “We must not neglect the word of God.
We should not stop preaching to serve food at tables.”
passages.original: Προσκαλεσάμενοι δὲ οἱ δώδεκα τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπαν Οὐκ ἀρεστόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς καταλείψαντας τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ διακονεῖν τραπέζαις

passages.text: Therefore, brothers, select from among you seven men confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will appoint this responsibility to them and will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”
passages.sermon:
The Twelve apostles spoke to the disciples.
They said, “Brothers, choose seven men from among you.
These men must have a good reputation.
They must be full of the Holy Spirit.
They must be full of wisdom.
We will put them in charge of this duty.
We ourselves will continue to pray.
We will continue to serve by teaching God’s word.”
passages.original: ἐπισκέψασθε δέ ἀδελφοί ἄνδρας ἐξ ὑμῶν μαρτυρουμένους ἑπτὰ πλήρεις Πνεύματος καὶ σοφίας οὓς καταστήσομεν ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ταύτης ἡμεῖς δὲ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ διακονίᾳ τοῦ λόγου προσκαρτερήσομεν

passages.text: This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, as well as Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.
passages.sermon:
The Twelve apostles spoke to all the disciples.
They gave a proposal to the group.
The whole group liked the proposal.
The group chose seven men.
Stephen was one of the men.
Stephen was full of faith.
Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit.
The group also chose Philip.
They chose Prochorus.
They chose Nicanor.
They chose Timon.
They chose Parmenas.
They chose Nicolas.
Nicolas was from Antioch.
Nicolas was a convert to Judaism.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤρεσεν ὁ λόγος ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους καὶ ἐξελέξαντο Στέφανον ἄνδρα πλήρης πίστεως καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Πρόχορον καὶ Νικάνορα καὶ Τίμωνα καὶ Παρμενᾶν καὶ Νικόλαον προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα

passages.text: They presented these seven to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
passages.sermon:
The believers chose seven men.
They brought these seven men to the apostles.
The apostles prayed for the seven men.
The apostles laid their hands on the seven men.
passages.original: οὓς ἔστησαν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προσευξάμενοι ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας

passages.text: So the word of God continued to spread. The number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly, and a great number of priests became obedient to the faith.
passages.sermon: God’s message spread.\r\nThe number of disciples in Jerusalem increased quickly.\r\nMany priests accepted the faith.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν μαθητῶν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ σφόδρα πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει

passages.text: Now Stephen, who was full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
passages.sermon:
Stephen was full of grace.
Stephen was full of power.
Stephen performed great wonders among the people.
Stephen performed great signs among the people.
passages.original: Στέφανος δὲ πλήρης χάριτος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐποίει τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἐν τῷ λαῷ

passages.text: But resistance arose from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, including Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and men from the provinces of Cilicia and Asia. They began to argue with Stephen, but they could not stand up to his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke.
passages.sermon:
Some men opposed Stephen.
These men belonged to the Synagogue of the Freedmen.
This synagogue included people from Cyrene.
It also included people from Alexandria.
It included people from Cilicia and Asia.
These men argued with Stephen.
Stephen spoke with great wisdom.
Stephen spoke by the power of the Holy Spirit.
The men could not stand up to Stephen’s wisdom.
The men could not stand up to the Spirit by whom Stephen spoke.
passages.original: ἀνέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς λεγομένης Λιβερτίνων καὶ Κυρηναίων καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων καὶ τῶν ἀπὸ Κιλικίας καὶ Ἀσίας συζητοῦντες τῷ Στεφάνῳ καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀντιστῆναι τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ τῷ Πνεύματι ᾧ ἐλάλει

passages.text: Then they prompted some men to say, “We heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.”
passages.sermon:
Some men acted under the direction of Stephen’s opponents.
These men made a statement about Stephen.
They said, “We heard Stephen speak blasphemous words against Moses.”
They also said, “We heard Stephen speak blasphemous words against God.”
passages.original: Τότε ὑπέβαλον ἄνδρας λέγοντας ὅτι Ἀκηκόαμεν αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ῥήματα βλάσφημα εἰς Μωϋσῆν καὶ τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: So they stirred up the people, elders, and scribes and confronted Stephen. They seized him and brought him before the Sanhedrin, where they presented false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.
passages.sermon:
Stephen was a Christian leader.
Some men opposed Stephen.
These men stirred up the people.
They also stirred up the elders.
They also stirred up the scribes.
They confronted Stephen.
They seized Stephen.
They brought Stephen before the Sanhedrin.
They presented false witnesses against Stephen.
The false witnesses spoke to the Sanhedrin.
The false witnesses said, “This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.”
passages.original: συνεκίνησάν τε τὸν λαὸν καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς καὶ ἐπιστάντες συνήρπασαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἤγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον Ἔστησάν τε μάρτυρας ψευδεῖς λέγοντας Ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος οὐ παύεται λαλῶν ῥήματα κατὰ τοῦ τόπου τοῦ ἁγίου τούτου καὶ τοῦ νόμου

passages.text: For we have heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to us.”
passages.sermon:
False witnesses spoke about Stephen.
They said, “We have heard him speak.”
He said, ‘Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place.’
He also said, ‘Jesus will change the customs.’
Moses gave us these customs.”
passages.original: ἀκηκόαμεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος οὗτος καταλύσει τὸν τόπον τοῦτον καὶ ἀλλάξει τὰ ἔθη ἃ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν Μωϋσῆς

passages.text: All who were sitting in the Sanhedrin looked intently at Stephen, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
passages.sermon:
The Sanhedrin was a council of Jewish leaders.
Many people sat in the Sanhedrin.
All of them looked closely at Stephen.
They saw Stephen’s face.
Stephen’s face looked like the face of an angel.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀτενίσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ καθεζόμενοι ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶδον τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ πρόσωπον ἀγγέλου
